# ECSS-Q-ST-70-12C, "Design rules for printed circuit boards", 14 July 2014

**What this file is.** A transcription of the clauses this project CITES, not a copy of the standard. The
document is published free of charge by the European Cooperation for Space Standardization and is fetched,
never redistributed here; what follows is the model, the constants and the worked example that
`tools/track_current.py` implements and tests itself against, with enough surrounding text to show what each
number is and is not. Anything this project does not use is not reproduced.

**Why this document and not IPC-2221 or IPC-2152 themselves.** Both IPC standards are paywalled and neither is
in this tree, which is why rule PI-001 has carried `source_status: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED` since the registry was
written: `dc_drop.py` has been judging every rail on this project's seven boards against an IPC-2221 formula
carried in a comment, from memory, with no document behind it. Annex D of this standard publishes closed-form
curve fits of BOTH IPC models with their constants, states the range each is valid over, and gives a worked
example that a tool can reproduce. It is an authority for the model, and it says plainly that the model this
project uses is the old one.

## D.1.1, the three models (transcribed)

> Track current rating can be computed with the following three commonly used models:
> - IPC-2221A. The original chart dated from the 1950's from National Bureau of Standards as shown in figure
>   6.4 IPC-2221A (also referenced in Appendix A7 of IPC-2152) This model has been superseded by IPC-2152.
> - IPC-2152 using the conductor sizing chart for vacuum and space environment in chapter 5.2.2 (dated August
>   2009).
> - CNES/QFT/IN.0113.
>
> The three models are similar for current rating computation. The CNES model is slightly more conservative
> than IPC-2152.

## D.1.2, the formulae (transcribed)

> a. In the three models the temperature increment of tracks is calculated with respect to the initial
>    temperature of the PCB when it is not powered.
> b. Current rating and cross sectional area are calculated in the three models by using the following
>    formulae:
>    1. Current rating [I in Amp]
>    2. Cross sectional area of tracks [A in mm2]
>    3. Temperature increment of tracks [dT in degC].
>    4. Constants k0, k1, m0, m1. The values of the constants are specified in the paragraphs describing each
>       model.
>    5. Conversion factor mm2 to mils2 c1=1550.
>    6. Formula for current rating:

```
I = k0 * dT^k1 * (c1 * A)^(m0 * dT^m1)
```

> 7. Formula for cross sectional area:

```
A = (1 / c1) * ( I / (k0 * dT^k1) )^( 1 / (m0 * dT^m1) )
```

## D.1.3, the worked example (transcribed)

> Using the mathematical model of IPC-2152 specified in clause D.2, to carry a current of 1 A and to maintain
> a temperature increment of 5 degC, a track of as-manufactured thickness of 25 um (as-designed thickness of
> 35 um, as per Table 7-1) should have an as-manufactured track width of 925 um (as-designed width of 975 um,
> as per Table 7-3).

This example is `track_current.py`'s selftest: the formula above with the D.2 constants returns 1.0001 A for
0.925 mm x 0.025 mm at 5 K, which is the standard's own number to four figures.

## D.2, IPC-2152 (transcribed)

> The IPC-2152 is the most comprehensive standard for the computation of the track current rating. It includes
> track sizing charts for vacuum or space environment, for several PCB thicknesses and for several copper
> plane thicknesses in SI (metric) and Imperial (inch) units. This standard allows to accurately calculate the
> current rating of a track from cross sectional area and the temperature rising of the track. However no
> derating are applied to take into account the complexity of the PCB.
> The model presented in this clause is based on a curve fitting performed on Figure 5-14 of chapter 5.2.2. of
> IPC-2152.
> c. The model is valid for a range up to 30 A and up to 100degC temperature increment with respect to an
>    initial PCB temperature of 25degC when not powered.
> d. ... constants: k0 = 0,0756   k1 = 0,4375   m0 = 0,5000   m1 = 0,0301

## D.3, CNES/QFT/IN.0113 (transcribed)

> The CNES current rating computation is based on the thermal model correlated to experimental data. The
> values obtained for current carrying capacity are about 10% more conservative with reference to those of
> IPC-2152. The model does not apply derating to take into account the complexity of the PCB.
> a. The model is derived from experimental data ranging up to 8 A and up to 100degC temperature increment
>    with respect to an initial PCB temperature of 25degC when not powered.
> b. ... constants: k0 = 0,0594   k1 = 0,4800   m0 = 0,5420   m1 = 0,0034

## D.4, IPC-2221A (transcribed)

> The model presented in this clause is based on a curve fitting performed on figure C for internal conductors
> of Figure 6-4 of IPC-2221A. IPC-2221A is the most conservative method of the three methods defined Annex D.
> Derating is not used in this model.
> a. The current rating is calculated with the following conditions:
>    1. I<0,7A for Trise 1 degC
>    2. I<0,9A for Trise 2 degC
>    3. I<1,0A for Trise 5 degC
>    4. I<1,2A for Trise 10 degC
>    Within these conditions the current rating is about 70% of the current rating calculated with IPC-2152.
> b. ... constants: k0 = 0,0240   k1 = 0,4393   m0 = 0,7252   m1 = 0,0002

## What this document does NOT settle for this project

1. **The external-conductor factor.** Annex D fits the INTERNAL conductor curve of IPC-2221A only (clause D.4
   says so in its first sentence). `dc_drop.py` uses `k = 0.048` for an outer-layer conductor, twice the
   internal 0.024, which is IPC-2221A's own external curve and is not reproduced anywhere in this document. So
   PI-001 is `PARTIALLY_VERIFIED`: the internal model is now sourced and the external factor is still this
   project's own number.
2. **The conditions attached to D.4.** The IPC-2221A fit is stated as valid only below 0.7 A at 1 K, 0.9 A at
   2 K, 1.0 A at 5 K and 1.2 A at 10 K. Several rails on these boards carry 6 to 18 A, which is far outside
   the range the standard puts on this model, and the standard's own remark is that IPC-2221A reads about 70
   percent of IPC-2152 inside it. `track_current.py` reports both numbers so the gap is visible rather than
   assumed.
3. **Derating.** Neither the IPC-2152 fit nor the CNES fit applies any derating for board complexity, and this
   standard says so of both. Whatever margin this project wants is this project's decision.
4. **Vacuum.** The IPC-2152 fit here is of the VACUUM and space-environment chart. This kit is a terrestrial
   field kit in a sealed case with no vents (owner ruling 7 September 2026), which is closer to the vacuum
   chart's no-convection assumption than a bench board in open air, but it is not the same thing and no claim
   is made that it is.
5. Everything else in the standard. Its annular ring, plating, spacing and qualification clauses are written
   for space hardware and are NOT this project's requirements; they are not transcribed and they are not cited.
